title: Terms of Account: Overdraft Protection Transfers on a Personal Checking Account
content:
A Personal Checking account may name one savings account as its overdraft protection source.

**Conditions on the link.**

1. The linked savings account must belong to the same owner as the checking account, matched on the owner recorded against the savings account.
2. The linked savings account must be in active status when the link is recorded.
3. The savings tier must be one the savings charter marks as eligible to act as an overdraft protection source.
4. Removing the link is always allowed.

**The transfer itself.** When a debit item would take the checking ledger balance below zero and a link exists, one transfer is made for that item in the exact amount of the shortfall, meaning the amount needed to bring the ledger balance to exactly zero after the item. The transfer is made only if the savings balance at that moment covers the whole shortfall; a partial transfer is never made. The transfer is recorded against the item it covered, and a matching withdrawal is taken from the savings account; whether that withdrawal counts toward the savings withdrawal allowance is decided by the savings charter.

**Charge on the transfer.** Each transfer incurs the checking tier's overdraft protection transfer charge, recorded against the transfer, limited to the tier's daily maximum of such charges per account per business day. A tier charge of 0.00 writes nothing.

**Effect on overdraft charges.** A covered item is not an overdraft and carries no charge for an item paid into overdraft.

**Worked illustration (hypothetical).** An item of 180.00 is presented against a checking ledger balance of 120.00. The shortfall is 60.00. Where the linked savings account holds 60.00 or more, exactly 60.00 moves across and the item is paid without an overdraft charge. Where it holds 45.00, nothing moves, because a partial transfer is never made.
